changelog:
The phone dashboard stopped being able to find the PC the longer the PC had been running, which is the "finding PC" that came back after everything seemed fine. Three separate faults were feeding each other.

The dashboard asked the relay for every announcement it still held rather than for recent ones. After one nine-hour session that was 2,532 messages and 645 KB, which a phone on mobile data could not download inside the three seconds it allowed itself. It now asks for the last half hour and gives the answer eight seconds to arrive.

The PC announced itself every ten seconds for as long as it ran whenever no dashboard had ever connected to it, which is exactly the situation when a phone is failing to connect. That is what built the pile the phone then choked on, so each hour of failure made the next attempt more certain to fail. It now announces quickly only when its address has just changed or a dashboard is genuinely reading it, and settles to once every ten minutes otherwise.

A tunnel that connected but never reported its address was waited on forever. The connection stays alive on its own keepalives, so nothing timed out and nothing retried: the PC sat there reachable by nobody, for as long as it was left running. It now gives up after a minute and builds a fresh tunnel, and it reads the address off the line that announces it rather than expecting one fixed domain name.
